text:
maria: Heads-up — noticed a ~20% tail latency regression on host-side request parsing after the KV-cache warmup change. Spike shows up when batching heuristics kick in + small streaming chunks.

alex: repro? which service/pool?

maria: rtx-dedicated pool. Repro curl attached, and a perf flame snapshot (short).

maria: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.dev/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' -d '{"model":"redwood-rtl-2048","input":"small prompt"}' --header 'Transfer-Encoding: chunked'

ken: TL;DR from perf: most extra time is host parse + smallwrite/grpc syscall overhead, not GPU. KV cache warmup path seems to force an early parse/utf8-normalize loop before chunk coalescing.

sam: can you paste the flame summary?

maria: here — top stacks: parse_proto::deserialize (34%), host_stream::coalesce (22%), grpc_writev_blocking (15%), kv_cache::prepare_prefix (12%), rest < 5%.

tina: interesting — parse_proto doing 34% is new. We patched prefix validation in #4432. Could that be triggering extra scans?

maria: looks like it. When batching heuristic queues multiple small requests we call prepare_prefix for each request synchronously which re-walks the buffer. Combined with smallwrite fragmentation = lots of syscalls.

alex: hypothesis: prepare_prefix should be async/deferred until we know framing is stable OR be cheap-cached per connection.

ken: also kernel selection plays a role: larger batch kernels assume contiguous token sequences; when host-side parsing fragments, we drop into fallback decode path which causes extra copy. That adds to host CPU.

sam: propose quick mitigations: 1) short-term canary — bypass prefix validation for small chunked requests in the canary pool; 2) medium-term — change batching heuristic to prefer coalescing before per-request KV warmup; 3) longer-term — make prepare_prefix incremental and attach to connection state.

maria: I opened a draft PR that implements (1) and a metric gate: if chunk_count < 3 && total_bytes < 2kb then skip prepare_prefix and mark metric "parse.skip_prefix". PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4551

tina: :thumbsup: Can we add a simple canary job? deploy-bot: starting canary on rtx-dedicated-canary (3 hosts) with image runtime:pr-4551

deploy-bot: canary started — 3 hosts, 1 hour ramp. Link: https://canary.redwood.dev/4551

ken: while canary runs, I'll prototype an incremental prefix cache. If we can memoize the first N bytes per-connection we avoid rewriting. Also consider bumping gRPC max_message_size to reduce fragmentation for tiny requests.

alex: bumping max_message_size helps in some cases but can increase memory footprint; prefer coalescing in the ingress proxy first.

sam: logging request sizes for the canary so we can correlate parse.skip_prefix with latency tail. maria can you add a quick hist for parse time binned by chunk_count?

maria: added metric and dashboard tile. Also added a synthetic load that mimics small chat-style requests + streaming.

tina: FYI, kernel-selection changes are also going out later today (kibana 8). If the canary shows improvement we can roll to the rest and then iterate on kernel heuristics to avoid fallback decode path.

maria: early canary numbers: p95 latency down ~12%, p99 down ~18% on rtx-dedicated-canary vs baseline in last 10m. CPU on hosts reduced by ~10%.

ken: promising. Next steps: 1) collect more canary data for 3h; 2) ken will PR incremental prefix cache; 3) alex will prototype batching heuristic change to prefer coalescing before KV warmup; 4) if stable, promote PR4551 to canary=50%.

sam: also add a small regression test in the perf harness that simulates fragmented chunked frames + KV warmup so we catch future regressions.

maria: agreed. I'll update the ticket with canary links and perf snapshots. Ticket: INF-1298.

tina: nice work catching this. :clap:

alex: thanks — ping if you need an extra pair of hands to vet the kernel fallback traces.

maria: will do. Closing the loop after 3h of canary data.

ken: FYI: if anyone is curious, snippet of the quick hack (in PR4551):

```
// skip expensive prefix work for tiny chunked requests
if (chunk_count < 3 && total_len < 2048) {
  metrics.incr("parse.skip_prefix");
  return;
}
```

maria: link to perf flame: https://perf.redwood.dev/flame/4928765432-sample

sam: nice. :rocket:
